Connect with `gcloud compute tpus tpu-vm ssh hy-nomas --zone=asia-northeast1-b -- -L 8790:127.0.0.1:8790` (your chip's name and zone) and open http://127.0.0.1:8790 on your own machine. models.name: TRELLIS.2
models.summary: Microsoft's open image-to-3D model: one RGBA picture in, a textured GLB mesh out, on a TPU v6e-1 VM (the model on the chip, the GLB export on the VM's CPU).
models.install: python3 -m pip install uv && python3 -m uv tool install --python 3.12 "mashbox[tpu,trellis-2]>=0.1.10" --with-executables-from huggingface_hub --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match

components.role: image encoder (gated by Meta; each user downloads it with their own login)

code (the GLB export's mesh simplification is a port of its simplify path; its remesh and mesh clean-up follow its documented behaviour, and the UV unwrap keeps the two steps of its uv_unwrap: chart clustering, then xatlas)
code (the sparse 3D convolution and the GLB export's texture sampling follow its op semantics and explicit-GEMM math)
code (stage 0's image resize and alpha handling reproduce the arithmetic of its 12.1.1.post0 release)
reference (the image encoder's layer math was checked against its DINOv3ViTModel definition; read, not copied)

First run on a new chip, load to ready: loading the weights and compiling, timed from the start of the load (weights on disk; the seconds before the load starts are not in it)
Programs compiled after ready, per run: new compile-cache entries from the chip stages and from the GLB export's JAX work on the VM's CPU together (so no run here is a warm run)
Chip memory peak

models.notes: Host memory: the whole command's VM maximum RSS was 72.9 to 89.1 GB per run here, out of the VM's 185.7 GB. A run of an earlier build of this port, on another picture, took 42 min 26.2 s and peaked at 122.9 GB, so plan for at least that much host memory and run one picture at a time.
